title: Generator Sizing Calculators | Wattlyst
meta: Generator calculators for home and appliances: running and starting watts, kVA size, AC and water pump loads, and fuel use, with each step shown.
author: ali-ahmad

sections.h2: Which generator calculator do I need?
p: For a whole home, start with the generator size calculator; for a list of appliances, the generator watts calculator. If a motor or compressor is on the list, the starting watts calculator and the guide to running vs starting watts show why it sets the size.

For one big load, use the generator size for a well pump or the generator size for an AC. If you already own a set, what a generator can run turns its kVA into usable watts, and the fuel consumption calculator gives the litres and rupees an hour.

l.t: generator size for a well pump

sections.h2: Why the starting surge decides the size
p: Running watts are what an appliance draws while it works; a motor or compressor draws several times that for a second or two as it starts. In the default home on the generator size calculator the running load is 3,017 W but the peak is 4,881 W, which is why it needs 6.5 kVA. Starting one motor at a time keeps the peak, and the generator, smaller.

faq.q: What size generator do I need for my house?
faq.a: 6.5 kVA for a typical home with fans, lights, an inverter fridge, a TV, one inverter AC and a water motor. More ACs or a non-inverter AC need more; enter your own list in the generator size calculator.

faq.q: How many watts does a kVA give?
faq.a: Usable watts are the kVA times one thousand times the power factor, about 80% on most sets, so a generator never carries its full kVA figure in watts. What a generator can run lists the usable watts for each size.

Petrol sets cover the small and middle sizes and cost less to buy; diesel is more common in the larger sizes and uses less fuel per unit of electricity. The fuel consumption calculator compares the running cost of both.

faq.q: Is a generator cheaper than solar or a UPS for backup?
faq.a: It depends on how many hours of backup you need a year. A generator is cheap to buy and costly to run; the UPS vs solar vs generator calculator compares the cost per backup hour over the years you pick.

l.t: UPS vs solar vs generator calculator

key_facts: Generator watts needed = the larger of (the running watts of every appliance on at once × 1.25) or (those running watts plus the starting surge of the one appliance with the biggest jump).
Generator starting watts = the running watts of everything on + the largest single starting jump; a second motor's surge is not added because two motors almost never start in the same second.
A generator's usable power in watts = nameplate kVA × 1,000 × power factor; at the usual 0.8 a 5 kVA set gives 4,000 W, a 3 kVA set 2,400 W and a 7.5 kVA set 6,000 W.

content.answer: Generator calculators size a set for what must run during a power cut: the running watts of everything on at once plus the starting surge of the largest motor, turned into kVA with the power factor and rounded up to a size that is sold. They also show what a given kVA can run and what it costs in fuel.
